platform: Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.36 test host; advertised archive floor 2.38)
observations: Each release was independently elaborated, compiled and verified. The reviewed route reconciled the ordinary route's public binding IR against fresh compiler output.

After deleting the producer project, the test moved the installed tree, linked a consumer with pkg-config and separately with the imported CMake target, and checked that all three shared libraries resolved inside that tree.
Blocking .get(), native co_await (including a separate host coroutine type), nested Routine<void>/Routine<T>, immediate tasks and descriptor-backed waits ran against real Lean tasks.
Exactly one outstanding stream demand, no prefetch, repeated exhaustion, early break, a returned Except.error item, typed step failure, cancellation during a pull and exactly-once cursor close.
IO start failure, typed EIO factory rejection, returned error-as-value and invalid arguments stay distinct. A signed 64-bit minimum, UTF-8 with embedded NUL and binary bytes survived the boundary.

Moved-from and consumed owners, duplicate waiters, rejected rvalue claims without loss of ownership, wrong thread and post-fork calls, worker-thread disposal, abandoned peer coroutine frames, late results and dispatcher shutdown.

sanitizer.instrumented: The installed C++ consumer and header-only dispatcher, not the bundled C/Lean shared libraries. Leak detection was not run.

scope: Local installed-package evidence for the Linux C++20 task profile. Not full-matrix acceptance for arbitrary-precision integers, resources, callback payloads, OS effects or other schedulers.
replay: Set LEAN_BRIDGE_CPP_TASK_REPLAY_DIR to the trusted release evidence directory containing ordinary/ and reviewed/, leave LEAN_BRIDGE_CPP_TASK_TEST unset, and run the same test file. It verifies, extracts, relocates, links and executes the two original archives without rebuilding Lean.
